title: Account Executive Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Under a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert an account executive salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, with fortnightly pay, tax, and super explained using Fair Work and ATO figures.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the typical account executive salary based on ABS average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 converts to an hourly rate of about $54.83 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an account executive salary from hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $50 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum pay for an account executive under Australian law?
faqs.a: If no award or enterprise agreement applies, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees receive an extra 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Many account executives are paid above these rates.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on an account executive salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy adds 2%. Use the ATO fortnightly tax table to work out withholding from each pay period.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding an Account Executive Salary in Australia

When evaluating an **account executive salary**, the most reliable method is to convert the offered annual figure to an hourly rate based on a standard 38-hour week. This approach lets you compare job offers, check against minimum legal entitlements, and estimate your take-home pay. The formula is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a 38‑hour week, that means hourly × 1,976 gives the annual gross pay.

### The 38‑Hour Week and the Fortnight

Most full‑time employees in Australia work 38 hours per week under the National Employment Standards. Many awards and agreements also use 38 hours as the ordinary hours base. When you see an **account executive salary** quoted as an annual figure, dividing by 1,976 (38 × 52) reveals the implied hourly rate. Conversely, if you have an hourly rate, multiplying by 1,976 gives the annual equivalent. The fortnightly pay is simply the weekly amount multiplied by two. For example, a $50 per hour rate yields $1,900 per week and $3,800 per fortnight before deductions.

### Minimum Pay and Award Coverage

Not all account executives are covered by an award. If no award or enterprise agreement applies, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, bringing the minimum to $33.05 per hour. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides that list minimum rates for each classification under specific awards. Some sales roles may fall under the Clerks Award or the Professional Employees Award, but many account executive positions are above‑award and rely on the National Minimum Wage as the floor.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are calculated on your ordinary earnings and paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an **account executive salary** of $100,000, the employer must contribute an additional $12,000 into your super fund. This amount is not deducted from your quoted salary; it is an extra cost to the employer. When comparing job offers, always check whether the salary is inclusive or exclusive of super.

### Using ABS Average Weekly Earnings as a Benchmark

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. For a 38‑hour week, that equates to an hourly rate of approximately $54.83. While this figure covers all occupations, it provides a useful reference point for an **account executive salary** in a typical full‑time role. Remember that actual pay varies widely by industry, experience, and location.

### Tax and Take‑Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates: no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy adds 2% on taxable income. The Australian Taxation Office provides fortnightly tax tables that employers use to withhold the correct amount. For example, an employee earning $1,900 per fortnight with the tax‑free threshold would have about $42 withheld (using the ATO’s table for 2024–26). Note that HELP debts, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

### How to Use This Information

Start by entering your hourly rate into [the timesheet](/) to see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. The tool includes a checkbox to add 25% casual loading if you are a casual employee. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool applies it on top. For award‑specific minimums, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets and super contribution caps.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
